title: 'Crypto King' or 'Lying King'? Aiden Pleterski says he was neither at alleged kidnappers' trial
summary: Aiden Pleterski denied ever calling himself the "Crypto King" — or paying for a Forbes sponsored article that did — under cross-examination at the trial for his alleged kidnappers in Toronto on…

image.caption: Under cross-examination Tuesday, Aiden Pleterski said he'd never promoted himself as the 'Crypto King.' (Evan Mitsui/CBC)

blocks.text: Toronto·New

Aiden Pleterski denied ever calling himself the "Crypto King" — or paying for a Forbes sponsored article that did — under cross-examination at the trial for his alleged kidnappers in Toronto on Tuesday.
Defence lawyer suggests Pleterski can't be trusted in cross-examination
"You weren't the Crypto King, you were the Lying King, you were taking other people's money and spending it on yourself," said defence lawyer Hussein Aly in Ontario Superior Court.
"I don't think I'm a king at all, and I disagree with that," replied Pleterski. He repeated in court that he'd never called himself the Crypto King even once.

Pleterski was convicted of fraud last month in connection with more than $30 million he took from investors to trade on their behalf, but he has yet to be sentenced. The 27-year-old told the court Tuesday he disagreed with that decision.

Akil Heywood, Alfredo Paladino and Rakeem Henry are all charged with kidnapping and extorting Pleterski over the course of three days in early December 2022. Pleterski testified to being beaten and tortured by his alleged kidnappers in various locations across southern Ontario as they questioned him about where his money was.

Alfredo Paladino, Akil Heywood and Rakeem Henry (from left to right) are accused of kidnapping and extorting the self-described 'Crypto King' Aiden Pleterski in December 2022. (Evan Mitsui/CBC, atlanticmastoronto/Instagram, Evan Mitsui/CBC)

The Crown alleges Heywood was one of Pleterski's investors who lost a significant amount of money and was the "driving force" behind the plan to kidnap him, while Paladino and Henry were allegedly involved in carrying it out.
Paladino and Henry are also charged with firearms offences, the aggravated assault of Pleterski, assaulting him with a weapon, and assault causing bodily harm over that same period.
All three men have pleaded not guilty.

blocks.text: Aly, who is representing Heywood, began his cross-examination of Pleterski Tuesday morning.

Before the court broke for lunch Tuesday, he'd called Pleterski the "Lying King" multiple times and ran the court through several examples of Pleterski's alleged lies from his fraudulent investment scheme and his bankruptcy proceedings.
Those included a screenshot of a $311 million fund Pleterski provided to investors, which Pleterski admitted never existed.

Defence lawyer Hussein Aly entered this screenshot as an exhibit at the trial for three men accused of kidnapping Aiden Pleterski. Pleterski admitted the $311 million never existed. (Ontario Superior Court of Justice)
"You're nothing but a liar, a cheat and a thief," said Aly to Pleterski in court. "Your religion is money. The only thing that matters to you in the world is money."
Pleterski denied both assertions.
Heywood's role in bankruptcy

The Crown entered copies of wire transfers and bank drafts as exhibits Tuesday morning showing that Heywood transferred Pleterski $300,000 in November 2021. And later, Pleterski's company transferred Heywood funds twice for a total of $250,000.
Aly also questioned Pleterski on how he ended up bankrupt in 2022.
"Your whole Ponzi scheme fell apart because someone went to the courts," he said to Pleterski.
Pleterski disagreed with calling it a Ponzi scheme, but said the "first two individuals who sued me were Sacha Singh and I believe Akil Heywood as well."
Aly said his client used lawful means to address his missing funds by taking Pleterski to court.
"You didn't go into bankruptcy, they forced you into bankruptcy," said Aly.
Again, Pleterski disagreed.
"You were mad at Akil Heywood, because of Heywood, no more private jets," said Aly.
Aiden Pleterski posted this photo of himself on a private jet to his own Instagram account. (aiden.ptrs/Instagram)

Earlier in his cross-examination Aly walked the jury through summaries of Pleterski's financial records which were used as evidence in his fraud trial and others from his bankruptcy. Those records showed he took in about $40 million dollars and spent over $13.5 million on lifestyle expenses, including on private jets and luxury cars.
Texts night of alleged kidnapping

Aly also entered a text message exchange between Pleterski's phone and Heywood's as an exhibit, which was time stamped 11:50 p.m. on Dec. 5, 2022. Based on the Crown's evidence at trial so far, and Pleterski's prior testimony, he said he was already kidnapped by that time that day.
This is a transcript of the text exchange:
Aiden Pleterski's phone: I have your money
Aiden Pleterski's phone: Don't worry ;)"
Aiden Pleterski's phone: Haha
Akil Heywood: I want it now
Aiden Pleterski's phone: Sorry for ripping u off for 7 mill
Aiden Pleterski's phone: But it's tough being a big bitch
Akil Heywood: Yup I agree

Pleterski testified he didn't send those text messages and said they would have been sent by "Slime" during the kidnapping. "Slime" was the lead kidnapper, according to the Crown, but he is not part of this trial.
Aly is expected to continue his cross-examination Tuesday afternoon.
